description: Add/drop, enrollment status, attendance and last date of attendance, grades, transcripts, and enrollment verifications in the SIS
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Enrollment status drives Title IV eligibility and disbursement; online terms start every 8 weeks; transcript and verification requests have external deadlines; an hour of lost grade or attendance entries must be re-keyed by faculty
manual_workaround: Printed class rosters; paper add/drop log keyed in after restore; enrollment verifications deferred
quantified_operational_impact: About 7,800 enrolled students; up to 1,200 add/drop transactions a day in the first week of a term
quantified_regulatory_impact: Enrollment status errors lead to incorrect Title IV disbursements and return-of-funds liabilities; records must be retained and retrievable (34 CFR 668.24)

description: Course delivery, assignments, discussions, academic activity records, and proctored exams in the LMS for 3,500 online students
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: All 3,500 online students stop at once; timed exams and 8-week terms leave little slack; academic activity records support attendance-based aid decisions; about $152,000 of online receipts per business day
manual_workaround: Extend deadlines; email course materials from faculty file copies; reschedule proctored exams; faculty log academic activity manually
dependent_third_parties: LMS vendor; proctoring vendor (AI-005); identity vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: Online faculty and instructional designers; online students
quantified_operational_impact: About 18,000 proctored exams a year (about 1,500 in a typical exam week); 12 hours down forces about 400 exam reschedules in an exam week
quantified_regulatory_impact: Academic activity records are evidence of attendance for Title IV return-of-funds calculations; accreditor distance education expectations

business_process: On-campus instruction, labs, and clinical rotations
description: Classroom and lab teaching, nursing simulation, and clinical placement clearances (immunizations, background checks) needed before students enter hospitals
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Classes can continue on paper for about 2 days; clinical sites refuse students whose clearance cannot be verified; about $248,000 of campus receipts per business day across 3 campuses
manual_workaround: Paper attendance; printed clearance roster sent to clinical sites weekly; labs run offline images
quantified_operational_impact: About 4,300 campus students; about 520 nursing students in clinical rotations each term
quantified_regulatory_impact: Clinical affiliation agreements require proof of clearance; accreditor attendance documentation

business_process: Title IV aid processing and disbursement
description: ISIR intake through SAIG, verification, packaging, Direct Loan origination, and disbursement records exchanged with the Department
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Cash: about $1.2 million of Title IV draws per business day during term-start peaks; disbursements must match enrollment; the third-party servicer works inside the FAMS; ISIRs can be re-requested from the Department
manual_workaround: Spare workstation with the Department-provided SAIG software; manual packaging for urgent cases; re-request ISIRs; delay non-urgent disbursements
dependent_systems: SYS-03; SYS-04; SYS-01; SYS-06; SYS-08 (integration platform)
dependent_third_parties: FAMS vendor; Department of Education systems; third-party servicer
dependent_people_or_facilities: Financial aid staff (28); Campus 1 financial aid office
quantified_operational_impact: About 9,000 aid recipients a term; 3 days down delays about $3.6 million of Title IV draws at term start
quantified_regulatory_impact: Administrative capability depends on timely and accurate Title IV administration (34 CFR 668.16); SAIG Enrollment Agreement terms

business_process: Student accounts and Title IV credit balance refunds
description: Tuition posting, payment plans, refund direct-deposit setup, and credit balance refunds paid to students for living expenses
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: A Title IV credit balance must be paid within 14 days (34 CFR 668.164(h)(2)); students depend on refunds for rent and food; about 9,000 refunds a year, concentrated in the first 3 weeks of each term
manual_workaround: Paper check run from the last refund file reconciled to the SIS ledger; emergency institutional grants for hardship cases; verify any bank change by phone
dependent_third_parties: SIS vendor; bank; payment plan vendor
quantified_operational_impact: Up to 1,800 refunds due in a term-start week; each day of delay pushes refunds toward the 14-day deadline
quantified_regulatory_impact: Missing the 14-day deadline is a Title IV finding; refunds diverted by fraud must be repaid to students

description: Inquiry response, applications, identity checks, acceptance, and handoff of admitted students to the SIS
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Online starts every 8 weeks; inquiries go cold within days; identity checks catch fraudulent applicants before aid is packaged
manual_workaround: Phone and paper applications; manual queue of inquiries; hold all new online applicants for identity review
quantified_operational_impact: About 4,000 online inquiries a month and about 450 new starts per online term; 3 days down near a start loses about 2% of starts
quantified_regulatory_impact: Fraud referral duty for applicants (34 CFR 668.16(g)) depends on identity check records

business_process: Campus emergency notification and physical security
description: Emergency mass notification by text, email, and voice; door access control; CCTV at 3 campuses
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: The college must immediately notify the campus community upon confirmation of a significant emergency (34 CFR 668.46(g)(1)); doors and cameras protect students and staff on site; contact lists sync nightly
manual_workaround: Public address and radio; campus safety officers in person; local alerting by phone tree; doors fail to locked with key override
dependent_third_parties: Emergency notification vendor; access control vendor; local law enforcement
quantified_operational_impact: About 4,900 people on campus at peak (students, faculty, staff)
quantified_regulatory_impact: Annual security report procedures under 34 CFR 668.46(g) must work as written; failures are Clery findings

description: Email, portal announcements, and messaging for 7,800 students and 600 employees
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Communications carry incident and class-change notices; the emergency notification service is separate (BP-07)
manual_workaround: Text alerts through the emergency notification service; phone trees; website banner
quantified_regulatory_impact: None beyond notice duties handled elsewhere

description: Service desk, password resets, MFA enrollment, and account recovery for students and staff
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Without account recovery, students locked out cannot attend online classes or exams; account recovery is also the main fraud path for portal takeover
manual_workaround: Identity-proofed phone resets by the service desk lead only; temporary passwords in sealed envelopes for campus labs
dependent_third_parties: Identity vendor; service desk tool vendor
quantified_operational_impact: About 900 student password and MFA requests a week at term start
quantified_regulatory_impact: Weak account recovery undermines 34 CFR 99.31(c) identity authentication and 314.4(c)(1)

business_process: Student success advising and early alert
description: Advisor caseloads, early-alert scores (AI-002), outreach, and referrals
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Outreach can pause for a week without lasting harm; scores are rebuilt from the data warehouse
manual_workaround: Advisors use SIS rosters and faculty referrals

description: Scheduling, crisis referral, and counseling treatment records at Campus 1 and by telehealth
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Students in crisis must reach a counselor or referral line; treatment records are confidential (FERPA treatment records exclusion)
manual_workaround: Crisis line by phone; paper intake; telehealth counselors call students directly
dependent_systems: SaaS counseling records application (SYS-15); SYS-06; SYS-07
dependent_third_parties: Counseling records vendor; telehealth counseling vendor
quantified_regulatory_impact: Treatment records must stay restricted to providers (34 CFR 99.3)

description: Enrollment and progress reports (with student consent), invoices, and the employer partner portal for 9 employer partners
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Partner contracts commit to 99.5% monthly portal availability and restoration within 24 hours; 2 hospital-system partners require SOC 2 Type 2 (P09); about 640 sponsored students
manual_workaround: Monthly reports and invoices sent as encrypted files from SIS extracts
dependent_systems: SYS-08 (employer partner portal, data warehouse); SYS-01; SYS-06
quantified_operational_impact: 9 partners; about 640 sponsored students; monthly invoicing of about $560,000
quantified_regulatory_impact: Disclosures to employers need written student consent (34 CFR 99.30)

description: Biweekly payroll for 600 employees, onboarding, and terminations
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Biweekly payroll; adjunct contracts start each term; terminations feed account removal
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll with adjustments; paper onboarding checklists
quantified_operational_impact: 600 employees; about 310 adjunct course assignments per term
quantified_regulatory_impact: Wage payment timing under state law

description: General ledger, vendor payments, Title IV fund reconciliation
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Month-end close and monthly Title IV reconciliation tolerate a week's delay

description: IPEDS, accreditor, Clery statistics, Title IV compliance audit support, and AI-002 model refresh
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: External reports have fixed due dates weeks out; the data warehouse can be rebuilt from SIS extracts
quantified_operational_impact: About 30 recurring external reports a year

description: Library catalog, e-resource access through SSO proxy, and tutoring center scheduling
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: E-resources can be reached through publisher sites; tutoring can be scheduled by phone
